intro.label: Convention Dining in San Diego
intro.title: Take the meeting out of the convention hall
intro.body1: Coco Maya is in Little Italy, north of the San Diego Convention Center within downtown San Diego. It is not positioned as the closest restaurant to the convention hall; it is a different downtown dining option for attendees who have enough time for a client meal, team dinner, happy hour, or hosted gathering outside the immediate convention blocks.
intro.body2: The right booking path depends on the schedule. A short break should prioritize proximity. A client lunch or executive dinner can justify leaving the convention area. Larger hosted groups may need dedicated space, coordinated service, AV, or centralized billing.

logistics.label: Convention Week Logistics
logistics.title: Choose the restaurant around the time you actually have
logistics.body1: If the team has less than an hour between sessions, staying close to the Convention Center is usually the operationally smarter choice. If the meal has a real business purpose—a client conversation, executive dinner, or hosted team gathering—Little Italy can provide a more distinct setting away from the trade-show floor.
logistics.body2: Build in time for session overruns, exiting the venue, rideshare pickup, downtown traffic, and guests arriving from different hotels. For client-facing meals, the host should plan to arrive first rather than scheduling the reservation against the exact end of a session.
